title: An ant nest dug into a soil bank, against the same bank with no nest in it
question: Ants now line the tunnels they dig, so a burrow stands instead of closing in five frames. One of these banks has 130 roofed tunnel cells and 125 cells of packed wall worked into it after 8,000 frames; the other has none at all — the ants dug twice as much there and every hole closed behind them. Can you tell which is which? And does the worked nest read as architecture, or as nothing? I made the packed wall DARKER than loose soil, which may be the wrong call: the inside of a bank is already dark, so the lining and the void it lines are the same brown. A pale wall like the nest material would read the opposite way.
context_md: Four stops per column, top to bottom: frames 0, 500, 2000, 8000. Held at noon, cropped to the face the colony works. Discrete events — lined: 278 digs, 384 wall cells packed, 130 roofed void standing. Ablated (PIXEL_PHYSICS_BURROW_LINING=off, same binary): 610 digs, 0 packed, 0 roofed void. The mechanic fires; the question is only whether it shows.
